policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: ASV 'its teeth' does not distinguish the qere from the ketiv; the note is classed alternative_rendering and therefore does not decide the reading.
ASV 'its back' is compatible with both the qere and ketiv forms and provides no mapped textual-variant note.
ASV 'a fourth beast' does not distinguish the qere and ketiv forms; the alternative-rendering note concerns 'terrible' and cannot decide this reading.
ASV 'with its feet' remains compatible with both readings; the only note is an unrelated alternative rendering of 'terrible'.
ASV 'among them' does not express the pronominal distinction between the qere and ketiv.
ASV 'three ... were plucked up by the roots' does not distinguish the qere and ketiv inflectional forms.
ASV 'before which' does not distinguish the qere from the ketiv pronominal form.
ASV 'thousands of thousands' permits both candidate forms and supplies no textual-variant note.
ASV 'ten thousand times ten thousand' does not distinguish the qere and ketiv forms and has no mapped textual-variant note.
ASV 'all of them' does not express the distinction between the qere and ketiv pronominal forms.
ASV 'whose teeth were of iron' does not distinguish the qere from the ketiv form.
ASV 'three fell' does not distinguish the qere and ketiv inflectional forms.
ASV 'before which' does not distinguish the qere from the ketiv pronominal form.
ASV 'The fourth beast shall be a fourth kingdom' does not distinguish the candidate forms; the note is classed alternative_rendering and concerns 'tread it down'.
ASV 'the Most High' is compatible with both candidate forms and provides no textual-variant note.
